record.title: Planting for heavy clay
record.why: "A rain garden for a terrace in Headingley" and "Planting for salt and wind at Craster" each tackle one difficult northern condition, but the most common one for gardens in the region has no piece of its own.
record.notes: Open on the spade that won't go in, or the boot left behind in March. Explain what clay is good for (it's fertile and holds water) before getting to how to work with it rather than against it. Then give a short list of plants that cope, using botanical names, cultivars and common-name glosses in the house style. [Need: plants the studio actually uses on clay, ideally from a named project.]
